recipes.name: Aunt Jules’ Balsalmic Chicken with Peppers
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons olive oil, or to taste
salt and black pepper to taste
1 green bell pepper, cut into strips
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 yellow bell pepper, cut into strips
1 large red onion, cut into strips
1 bunch fresh asparagus spears, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
0.33333334326744 cup balsamic vinegar, or to taste

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium heat, and drizzle the olive oil into the hot skillet. Cook and stir 4 garlic cloves just until fragrant, about 1 minute, smashing them into the oil with a spoon as you stir. Sprinkle the chicken breasts with salt and pepper, and brown them in the hot oil until the surface is golden and the meat is no longer pink inside, 5 to 8 minutes per side. Remove the chicken breasts to a platter and keep warm.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in the skillet over medium heat, and scrape up any browned bits of flavor from the bottom of the skillet. Stir in 2 more cloves of garlic, the green, red, and yellow bell peppers, red onion, and asparagus, and cook and stir until the vegetables are brightly colored and softened, about 10 minutes. Toss the spinach leaves with the hot vegetables to just wilt the spinach. Divide the cooked vegetables between 4 serving plates, and top each plate with a chicken breast.

Stir the balsamic vinegar and brown sugar into the skillet over medium-low heat, stirring until the vinegar comes to a full boil and the sugar has dissolved. Cook the mixture until reduced and thickened, 3 to 5 minutes; spoon the balsamic sauce over each chicken breast to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Aunt Jules’ Balsalmic Chicken with Peppers
raw_recipe.description: Bright green, red, and yellow peppers are lightly cooked with fresh asparagus and spinach, then served with a browned chicken breast topped with a sweet, simple balsamic sauce.

review.reviewBody: I have made many recipes from this site and never rated any before, but this one I must comment on. Absolutely delicious! So quick and easy, it's hard to believe it tastes so good -- and healthy too! I doubled the amount of balsamic, but not the brown sugar, and served it over yellow rice. This will be a regular in our house!

Yummy ! but made a couple of changes with what I had on hand. First of all I used chicken thighs, seasoned, browned in garlic oil then placed in 350 oven while I made the veggies. Didnt have asparagus so i subbed brussel sprouts cut in half, didnt have a yellow pepper so threw in a few assorted peppers from the garden, doubled the sauce using 1/3 c balsamic and 1/3 cup of some raspberry vinegar I grabbed at the local farmers market.Didn't have baby spinach so I used Swiss Chard. Used a bit more garlic than the recipe suggested because, well garlic ;) deglazed the pan after browning the chicken with a touch of Marsala wine. Served with mashed potatoes. Definitly a Keeper :) I feel like this recipe would work with any sort of veggies you have sitting around, especially mushrooms * One more thing, I drizzled a bit of the sauce on the thighs and set it under the broiler to crisp up the skin. Make sure to dbl. the sauce recipe as suggested ! Enjoy ! ** Might try adding a couple of drops of liquid smoke or do the chicken on the grill sometime for variation

I should have trusted my instincts. This recipe turned out very bland. That's why everyone is saying to double or triple the sauce because it is the only item in the dish with any flavor. I ended up seasoning my veggies with tumeric, salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, and paprika. I also served the dish with mozzarella cheese pearls in addition to the balsamic glaze. If I make this again, I would half the spinach and add some roasted grape tomatoes. This recipe has potential to be fantastic and healthy. It just needs a lot more seasoning to make it palatable. Another note: do not overcook the balsamic glaze. If you overcook it, it will become a caramel or toffee consistency and stick to your teeth. Lucky for me, I have a store-bought balsamic glaze I keep around as back-up.

Excellent!!!! I was skeptical at first about the amount of balsamic vinegar called for this dish. Then, after I read a few reviewers and some people said that they doubled the sauce, I decided to give it a try. I browned the chicken first and set aside, then sautéed the onions, garlic and vegetables (I only had green/red bell peppers and onions on hand), then all other ingredients along with ½ cup of chicken broth and added everything in my crockpot for a couple of hours. Served over Basmati brown rice.

Love all of the veggies! Good balance between the veg and protein. I made one change and cut the chicken into strips also. My other change was to add everything back to the pan after the balsamic step and tossed it in the sauce in the pan. I felt it needed a bit of a kick so I added some sambal oelek to my plate but hot peppers in oil would have worked as well or even Sriracha. Bonus points for a one pan dish! Thank you for sharing your recipe MellyBelly.

DELICIOUS!!! This will be a regular meal in my house. Everyone loved it. I did add mushrooms, added a lot more garlic (about a head and half) and tripled the sauce as suggested by other reviewers. I also seasoned the chicken breast’s with garlic powder and onion powder along with the salt and pepper and a spritz of balsamic on each breast. OMG this is absolutely delicious!!!!

This was EXCELLENT!! great mixing of flavors. I do recommend to triple or quadruple sauce...but I am a sauce person...great job!! Also, I put more spinach and used the veggies and spinach as bed did not have to make rice or anything else with it!! Thanks!

Made it with organic scarlet kale instead of spinach and no red onion and it was excellent! My wife and I thought it tasted like something you'd get at an upscale restaurant. I placed it on a base of organic basmati rice, so I made 50% more balsamic vinegar mixture. I will definitely be making this again.
Definitely increase the sauce.. sooo good! I doubled the balsamic but used one tablespoon of sugar. I’ll prob triple the balsamic next time and double the sugar

Last night I was browsing the AllRecipes site for a healthy chicken recipe simply to use up some extra veggies I had on hand, and also because I didn't want to stop at the store. So I came upon this recipe. My husband and I love balsamic vinegar, so I figured this recipe would be "okay" and would at least fill our hungry bellies. Was I ever wrong... OMG - instead of "okay" it was wonderful. A real keeper! I didn't change anything about the recipe, EXCEPT that I used up the vegetables that I had on hand. As I didn't have asparagus or a green pepper at home, I didn't use those. I used one orange pepper, one red pepper and one yellow pepper. I had fresh mushroom to use up, so I sliced up about a cup and a half of mushrooms and used those. I also didn't have a red onion, but I had a large vidalia, so that sucker went into the veggie saute as well. Oh, and since we love balsamic, I did double the sauce since I'd read other reviews that did the same. Good thing I did -- my husband was dipping his bread into the leftover sauce, it's sooooooo good. Funny, I came upon this recipe in an effort to simply "use up" extra peppers and mushrooms, and discovered a recipe that we will definitely be enjoying time and again in the future. Thanks MellyBelly (and your Aunt Jules)!!! :o)
this was a very good recipe. healthy and very flavorful. I use balsamic fig with the brown sugar we loved it!

Since I am not a fan of balsamic vinegar I was reluctant to try this. But I had peppers and chicken on hand that needed to be consumed. I cut the chicken into strips, added yellow squash and did without the asparagus and spinach. Other than that, I followed the recipe. The flavors were sweet and tangy so it worked out okay! I'll be making it again. :-)

Chicken tasted delicious & tender. Next time I will double the basalmic sauce - it was tasty. Made rice pilaf as suggested. Did not like the choice of mixed vegetables. Otherwise, I will make the chicken once again.

The recipe was easy to follow. The only change I made was to season the veggies with the balsamic vinaigrette and a little 
syrup (I had no brown sugar) in the skillet before serving. It was delicious.
Well, this was a bit of a disappointment, especially given the prep time. Of course, we were comparing this to the Chicken Veracruz recipe, which has similar ingredients but much more tasty.
Finished dish needs more sauce. I will try it again
I made this dish and it came out perfect. Thanks!!
It was so good! Quick and fast
